extracted.intended_audience: social science and humanities researchers, repository operators, and scholarly publishing stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the policies, technical design, and operational practices of a preprint/archive platform (here: SocArXiv) with respect to copyright, preservation, moderation, metadata, and post-publication review support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright posting rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may not legally post versions of content that they do not have the right to post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally authors are free to post the author’s original version (preprint) and may post accepted manuscripts after embargoes and restrictions set by publishers; final published versions typically require a license or payment. Platform operators and users should understand publisher policies before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement versus policy wording
rubrics_metrics.description: A platform's stated copyright policy may be unchanged, but enforcement intensity can change (e.g., post-acquisition clean-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between the written policy and the site's desire/ability to enforce it. Expect more aggressive enforcement when a commercial publisher with its own sharing policies acquires or manages a site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe Harbor and takedown responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe Harbor laws allow hosting sites to claim ignorance of user-posted infringing content but require removal upon notification by the copyright holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites relying on safe harbor must act expeditiously on legitimate takedown notices; they should have clear takedown procedures. Note: by law, a copyright owner’s notice does not require the owner to 'prove' copyright in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission / submission checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the platform reviews submissions for potential copyright violations at the time of ingest (human or automated checks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options range from no checking (accept everything) to automated ingestion checks to human review verifying the poster's authority to post attachments; consider trade-offs between protection and throughput.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit workflow and metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission interface requirements (e.g., include title in subject line, abstract in message body; affiliation may or may not be required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design deposit processes to capture essential metadata; clarify what is required vs optional and ensure automated parsing behaves as users expect (avoid surprising profile data parsing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and content types hosted
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the service is strictly a 'preprint server' or a broader archive hosting working papers, preprints, published PDFs, data, code, and other research components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about accepted content types. Ambiguity (calling a service a preprint server while hosting published PDFs) causes confusion and legal risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform openness (open-source/open-access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform should be open-access and ideally open-source (the page notes SocArXiv is 'open-access, open-source').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-source code and open-access hosting support community trust and potential migration; makes it easier for community-controlled alternatives to commercial platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata openness and linking data/code
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform should encourage linking and sharing of data and code and serve research to an open metadata system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for linking components (data, code, preprints) and exposing open metadata enhances reuse, discovery, and integration with post-publication review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for post-publication peer review and community curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform should provide the foundation for post-publication review systems and let communities organize their own peer-review and publication activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features to allow commenting, community-organized review groups, and selection/publishing workflows are desirable; make clear how community reviews relate to formal journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent identifiers and permanence claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide persistent IDs for deposited items (SocArXiv provided an osf.io URL as a 'persistent ID').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer DOIs or other stable resolver-based identifiers over plain URLs; document preservation/back-up measures and the guarantees behind 'persistence' (e.g., preservation funds, LOCKSS, institutional commitments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and sustainability planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for long-term preservation and fund ongoing operating expenses (arXiv example: >$820,000/year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify funding sources (university hosts, grants, donations), preservation mechanisms (funds, institutional partners, LOCKSS), and contingency plans if funding ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about governance and business plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear public documentation of who is behind the service, governance structure, business plan, and where 'temporary' interfaces lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission pages should link to project descriptions, steering committee information, contact emails, and fundraising/operational plans to build trust and reduce confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of terminology and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about version distinctions (preprint, accepted manuscript, version of record) and align with community standards (e.g., NISO vocabulary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sloppy use of terms; explain which 'versions' are appropriate to deposit and how version metadata will be recorded and displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment of legal posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize legal risks of relying solely on terms-of-use and safe-harbor defenses, especially if affiliated with a major university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions described as 'hosts' or 'programs' may invite different expectations and legal exposure; have explicit takedown and legal response policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation versus human moderation trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether deposit and ingestion are automated or involve human processing, and what checks humans perform (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated ingestion scales but may permit inappropriate uploads; human moderation can prevent some abuses but is costly and slows deposits. Document which approach is used and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: User advice and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise authors to proceed with caution, keep backup copies, and be mindful about what they post during a platform's early/temporary phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate best practices to users (retain local copies, verify copyright status, consider DOIs/registrations) especially during rapid launches or temporary interfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link rot and discovery considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the difference between preservation of content and long-term discoverability of URLs; URLs can be fragile compared to DOIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt best practices for persistent identifiers and archiving, and explain how the system will ensure both preservation and discovery if the host domain changes or the service migrates.
